headline: Microsoft unveils Maia 300, an AI chip built for inference
dek: Microsoft claims 40% more tokens per megawatt than leading GPU systems, per Canaltech and TechRadar.

s2.label: What happened
s2.title: A new chip for answering
body: Microsoft revealed the Maia 300 on Monday, an accelerator for AI inference (running a trained model to answer prompts) in its own data centers. It succeeds the Maia 200, launched in January (Canaltech, TechRadar).
Microsoft says the chip processes 40% more tokens per megawatt than leading GPU-based systems. Deployment is set to begin in 2027 (Canaltech, TechRadar).

s3.label: How it works
s3.title: Chiplets, memory and racks
s3.body: The design targets long conversations, multi-step reasoning and agents that chain actions (Canaltech, TechRadar).

points.t: Smaller blocks on TSMC's N2P process split compute, memory control and communication, keeping data near where it is processed (Canaltech, TechRadar).
Each accelerator carries 288 GB of HBM4 memory with up to 18 terabytes per second of transfer speed (Canaltech).
A rack holds 96 accelerators and can push up to seven times the token throughput of a Maia 200 rack (Canaltech, TechRadar).

s4.label: Why it matters
s4.title: Efficiency is the target
body: Tokens are the units of text a model reads and writes. Tokens per megawatt measure how many answers a chip delivers for each unit of power, a metric Microsoft is pushing as AI electricity use climbs (Canaltech, TechRadar).

The Maia 200 already runs production workloads for Microsoft 365 Copilot and Microsoft's own models. TechRadar says Microsoft credits it with up to 1.7 times more tokens per watt than leading GPU infrastructure.

stat.cap: more tokens per megawatt, per Microsoft

items.t: GitHub Copilot and Microsoft Foundry are expected to start running on Maia 300 by the end of this year (TechRadar).
Microsoft plans to begin deploying the chip in its data centers, as part of a push toward multi-gigawatt capacity (Canaltech, TechRadar).
Pricing and any sale to outside customers were not reported by Canaltech or TechRadar.

caption.hook: Microsoft unveiled Maia 300, an AI inference chip it says delivers 40% more tokens per megawatt than leading GPU systems.
body: Canaltech and TechRadar report that the chip arrives less than a year after the Maia 200, which debuted in January. TechRadar adds that each Maia 300 runs within a 950-watt thermal envelope, and a full 96-accelerator rack within a 167 kW power budget.

According to TechRadar, the accelerators link over high-bandwidth connections built for tensor parallelism, which splits one model's work across several chips, plus a custom AI transport layer on Ethernet.
Microsoft's announcement did not address pricing or outside sales, the outlets say.
